Chapter 3: Discovering “Must”—Listening to the Inner Voice and Honoring Passion.
You know, while “Should” is shaped by everything around us—our families, society, expectations—“Must” is something entirely different. It comes from deep within. It's that quiet, persistent voice you might barely hear, the one that somehow just knows what brings you joy, what feels meaningful, and what makes hours slip away without you even noticing.
Here’s the thing: “Must” isn’t always loud or obvious. Sometimes, it’s just a faint whisper, almost drowned out by the everyday noise of life. But even if you lose track of it, it’s always there, waiting for you to pay attention.
Let me share a story. Imagine someone who’s worked in finance for years. On the surface, everything looks perfect—steady promotions, praise from bosses, the works. But inside, there’s this growing emptiness. Then, during a vacation, a chance meeting with a street artist brings back memories of childhood afternoons spent drawing. And suddenly, it’s like coming home. The feeling is so real, it’s almost physical.
For a lot of people, the journey toward “Must” starts with simple acts of curiosity. Maybe you sign up for a pottery class, dust off an old camera, or lose yourself in a favorite book for an afternoon. These moments are easy to brush off as just hobbies or distractions. But if you pay attention, they’re actually clues—tiny signposts pointing you toward something deeper.
Choosing “Must” isn’t about making grand gestures or turning your whole life upside down. It’s about honoring what feels true, even in the smallest ways. One person might wake up just an hour earlier to write before work. Someone else might carve out a tiny corner in the living room just for painting. Over time, those little acts build up. They create momentum—and suddenly, new possibilities start to appear.
But let’s be honest: “Must” usually comes with a whole lot of uncertainty. There are no guarantees of success, no clear roadmap, and nobody promising you approval. Choosing “Must” can feel risky—sometimes, even reckless. It takes trust. You have to trust yourself, trust the process, and believe your passion is worth following, even when the outcome isn’t clear.
It’s so easy to fall into the habit of waiting for permission—waiting for someone to choose you, to validate your dream, to tell you it’s okay to go for it. But that’s not how “Must” works. It’s a choice only you can make, from the inside out. The world might never flash a big sign saying, “Now’s the time.” The only way forward is to listen, to trust, and to act anyway.
One artist described choosing “Must” as both terrifying and exhilarating. There were doubts, plenty of rough days, and times when the old life of “Should” seemed so much easier. But there was also this incredible sense of being alive—a feeling of being fully engaged with the world. Little by little, the fear faded. In its place? A quiet, steady confidence.
Here’s what’s important: the journey toward “Must” looks different for everyone. There’s no perfect map, no one-size-fits-all formula. What really matters is your willingness to listen, to try things out, to make mistakes, and—most importantly—to keep going. Passion isn’t something you stumble upon overnight. You discover it by taking action, experimenting, and having the courage to begin, even when you’re not sure where you’ll end up.
